report.summary: Chunk defines _infer_paths, prepare_task, main; imports from sibling modules; no docstrings/claims with checkable assertions.
risks: _infer_paths | medium | Uses heuristic 'looks_like_path' based on '/' or '\\' or '.' in name; may miss or misidentify paths. | Test with edge cases (e.g., version strings with dots, absolute paths without dot).
prepare_task | medium | Calls enqueue with no error handling; if enqueue fails, queued_path remains None but no exception raised. | Check if enqueue can fail and how caller should handle it.
main | low | Prints JSON to stdout; no error handling for prepare_task exceptions. | Add try/except or document expected failure modes.

handoff.purpose: Defines task preparation logic: path inference, task preparation with memory and optional Claude enqueueing, and CLI entry point.

symbols.name: _infer_paths
symbols.note: Heuristic path extraction from text; checks existence via Path.exists().

symbols.name: prepare_task
symbols.note: Resolves repo root, loads project, infers paths, routes task, records memory event, optionally enqueues Claude request. Returns dict with results.

symbols.name: main
symbols.note: CLI entry point that parses arguments and calls prepare_task, printing JSON result.

claims.text: Prepare a user task for Codex/Claude collaboration.
claims.why: The description refers to overall program purpose; the code does prepare a task and optionally enqueues for Claude, but 'collaboration' is not explicitly verified.

claims.text: single routes one task; spawn lets Ikarus decompose and fan out
claims.why: The strategy parameter is passed to enqueue but its effect is not defined in this chunk; relies on external implementation.

observations.what: _infer_paths uses a simple heuristic to detect paths; may include non-path tokens (e.g., 'a/b' in a version string) or miss paths without '.' or '/'.
prepare_task calls enqueue with 'objective' derived from message; no validation that enqueue succeeds or that the returned path is valid.
main prints JSON to stdout; no error handling for exceptions from prepare_task or json.dumps.
